title: A Crowd-Audited Atlas of Implicit Bias in LLM-Powered Agents
abstract: arXiv:2611.21376v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Prior work has shown that large language models (LLMs) express implicit biases in high-publicity, one-off decision scenarios such as hiring and intelligence assessment. However, as people increasingly employ autonomous, LLM-powered AI agents that make decisions on their behalf in doing day-to-day tasks, it is of critical importance that we understand how implicit biases, based on sociodemographic assumptions, emerge across a broad milieu of workaday decision scenarios. We used the 17 domains of daily activity in the American Time Use Survey (ATUS) to generate an atlas of 506 decision scenarios in which LLMs --- endowed with personas representing different races, gender identities, and political ideologies --- expressed significant implicit bias. translated_title: 《LLM驱动的智能体中隐性偏见的众包审计图谱》
translated_abstract: 先前的研究表明，大型语言模型（LLM）在高关注度、一次性的决策场景（如招聘和智力评估）中会表现出隐性偏见。然而，随着人们越来越多地使用自主的、由LLM驱动的AI智能体来代表自己完成日常任务，理解基于社会人口统计学假设的隐性偏见如何在广泛的日常决策场景中产生变得至关重要。我们利用美国时间使用调查（ATUS）的17个日常活动领域，生成了一个包含506个决策场景的图谱，在这些场景中，被赋予代表不同种族、性别认同和政治意识形态的人设的LLM表现出了显著的隐性偏见。接着，在一项众包审计中，500名参与者对哪些存在隐性偏见的决策场景最值得进一步审查做出了8,010次二元选择。我们发现参与者优先考虑了……（原文摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 该研究基于美国时间使用调查（ATUS）的17个日常活动领域构建了包含506个决策场景的图谱，揭示LLM智能体在不同种族、性别认同和政治意识形态人设下表现出显著隐性偏见，并通过500名参与者、8,010次二元选择的众包审计来确定最值得进一步审查的偏见场景。
en_tdlr: This study builds an atlas of 506 decision scenarios across 17 ATUS daily activity domains revealing significant implicit bias in LLM agents with personas of different races, gender identities, and political ideologies, and conducts a crowdsourced audit with 500 participants making 8,010 binary choices to identify which biased scenarios most deserve further review.
